[2026-07-19T23:39:54.026Z] [INFO]         "content": "/**\n * Pure helpers for the `/fix --ci-cd` command (issue #1733).\n *\n * `/fix --ci-cd <repository>` automatically:\n *   1. detects the languages used in the target repository,\n *   2. inspects the latest default-branch commit and its CI/CD runs,\n *   3. creates a remediation issue (mirroring the `/task` issue-creation flow)\n *      that links the language-appropriate CI/CD pipeline templates and the\n *      CI/CD best-practices guide, and\n *   4. hands the issue off to\n *      `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge`, forwarding every\n *      option that `/fix` itself does not consume (e.g. --tool, --model,\n *      --think).\n *\n * The issue title and body are taken from the standard prompt in\n * https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/139, omitting the\n * its retired case-study paragraph in favor of `--development-log` and omitting\n * paragraphs that `--deep-analysis` already injects into the AI prompt (issue\n * #1733) — see `buildStandardPromptParagraphs` below.\n *\n * Everything that does not touch the network or the filesystem lives here so it\n * can be unit-tested without GitHub access.\n */\n\nimport { KEEP_WORKING_PROMPT } from './solve.keep-working.detect.lib.mjs';\n\n/**\n * Canonical mapping from GitHub Linguist language names to the\n * link-foundation AI-driven-development pipeline templates.\n *\n * Order in this array is the stable tie-breaker when two languages contribute\n * an equal number of bytes. Accepts:\n *   - https://github.com/owner/repo (with optional .git / trailing slash)\n *   - github.com/owner/repo\n *   - owner/repo shorthand\n * Rejects anything that points deeper than a repository (issues, pulls, …),\n * contains whitespace, or is otherwise malformed.\n */\nexport function parseFixRepository(value) {\n  const candidate = String(value || '')\n    .trim()\n    .replace(/^[<([{]+/, '')\n    .replace(/[>\\])}.,;:]+$/, '');\n  if (!candidate || /\\s/.test(candidate)) return null;\n\n  // Normalize away an optional protocol, then require either a github.com host\n  // or a bare `owner/repo` shorthand. Any other host is rejected.\n  let withoutProtocol = candidate.replace(/^https?:\\/\\//i, '');\n  const hadProtocol = withoutProtocol !== candidate;\n\n  let pathPart;\n  if (/^github\\.com\\//i.test(withoutProtocol)) {\n    pathPart = withoutProtocol.replace(/^github\\.com\\//i, '');\n  } else if (!hadProtocol && !withoutProtocol.includes('.com/') && !/[^/]+\\.[^/]+\\//.test(withoutProtocol)) {\n    // Bare shorthand like `owner/repo`.\n    pathPart = withoutProtocol;\n  } else {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  pathPart = pathPart.replace(/\\.git$/i, '').replace(/\\/+$/, '');\n\n  const segments = pathPart.split('/').filter(Boolean);\n  if (segments.length !== 2) return null;\n\n  const [owner, repo] = segments;\n  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/.test(owner) || !/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/.test(repo)) return null;\n\n  return {\n    owner,\n    repo,\n    fullName: `${owner}/${repo}`,\n    url: `https://github.com/${owner}/${repo}`,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Normalize the GitHub `/languages` response (a `{ \"JavaScript\": bytes }` map)\n * or an array of names into a byte-sorted array of `{ name, bytes }`.\n */\nexport function normalizeLanguages(input) {\n  let entries = [];\n  if (Array.isArray(input)) {\n    entries = input.map(name => [String(name), 0]);\n  } else if (input && typeof input === 'object') {\n    entries = Object.entries(input).map(([name, bytes]) => [String(name), Number(bytes) || 0]);\n  }\n  return entries\n    .filter(([name]) => name)\n    .map(([name, bytes]) => ({ name, bytes }))\n    .sort((a, b) => b.bytes - a.bytes || a.name.localeCompare(b.name));\n}\n\n/**\n * Map detected languages to CI/CD templates, sorted so that the templates for\n * the most-used languages come first (issue #1733: \"links to CI/CD templates\n * should be sorted by detected languages in the target repository\").\n *\n * Returns:\n *   - sortedTemplates: matched templates ordered by aggregate detected bytes\n *   - unmatchedLanguages: detected languages with no template (informational)\n */\nexport function mapLanguagesToTemplates(languages) {\n  const normalized = normalizeLanguages(languages);\n\n  const templateByLanguage = new Map();\n  for (const template of CI_CD_TEMPLATES) {\n    for (const language of template.languages) {\n      templateByLanguage.set(language.toLowerCase(), template);\n    }\n  }\n\n  const aggregate = new Map(); // template.key -> { template, bytes, languages: [] }\n  const unmatchedLanguages = [];\n\n  for (const { name, bytes } of normalized) {\n    const template = templateByLanguage.get(name.toLowerCase());\n    if (!template) {\n      unmatchedLanguages.push(name);\n      continue;\n    }\n    const existing = aggregate.get(template.key) || { template, bytes: 0, languages: [] };\n    existing.bytes += bytes;\n    existing.languages.push(name);\n    aggregate.set(template.key, existing);\n  }\n\n  const templateOrder = new Map(CI_CD_TEMPLATES.map((template, index) => [template.key, index]));\n  const sortedTemplates = [...aggregate.values()].sort((a, b) => b.bytes - a.bytes || templateOrder.get(a.template.key) - templateOrder.get(b.template.key));\n\n  return { sortedTemplates, unmatchedLanguages };\n}\n\n/**\n * Title of the auto-generated remediation issue, taken exactly from the\n * standard template issue https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/139\n * (issue #1733: \"use title and description exactly\"). The issue is created in\n * the target repository itself, so it carries no repository suffix.\n */\nexport const CI_CD_ISSUE_TITLE = 'Check for all false positives, false negatives, warnings and errors in CI/CD and fix them all';\n\nexport function buildCiCdIssueTitle() {\n  return CI_CD_ISSUE_TITLE;\n}\n\nfunction shortSha(sha) {\n  return String(sha || '').slice(0, 7);\n}\n\n/** Render the detected-languages section. */\nexport function buildLanguagesSection(languages) {\n  const normalized = normalizeLanguages(languages);\n  if (normalized.length === 0) {\n    return 'No languages were reported by the GitHub Linguist API for this repository.';\n  }\n  const total = normalized.reduce((sum, { bytes }) => sum + bytes, 0) || 1;\n  const lines = normalized.map(({ name, bytes }) => {\n    const percent = ((bytes / total) * 100).toFixed(1);\n    return `- **${name}** — ${percent}%`;\n  });\n  return lines.join('\\n');\n}\n\n/** Render the recommended-templates section, sorted by detected languages. */\nexport function buildTemplatesSection(languages) {\n  const { sortedTemplates, unmatchedLanguages } = mapLanguagesToTemplates(languages);\n  const lines = [];\n\n  if (sortedTemplates.length === 0) {\n    lines.push('No language-specific template matched the detected languages. Review all templates and apply the closest match:');\n    lines.push('');\n    for (const template of CI_CD_TEMPLATES) {\n      lines.push(`- ${template.label}: [${template.repo}](${templateUrl(template.repo)})`);\n    }\n  } else {\n    lines.push('Apply the best practices from these templates, in priority order (most-used language first):');\n    lines.push('');\n    sortedTemplates.forEach((entry, index) => {\n      const detected = entry.languages.join(', ');\n      lines.push(`${index + 1}. **${entry.template.label}** — [${entry.template.repo}](${templateUrl(entry.template.repo)}) _(detected: ${detected})_`);\n    });\n  }\n\n  if (unmatchedLanguages.length > 0) {\n    lines.push('');\n    lines.push(`Other detected languages without a dedicated template: ${unmatchedLanguages.join(', ')}.`);\n  }\n\n  return lines.join('\\n');\n}\n\n/** Render the CI/CD runs section from the GitHub Actions API payload. */\nexport function buildRunsSection(runs, { emptyMessage } = {}) {\n  const list = Array.isArray(runs) ? runs : [];\n  if (list.length === 0) {\n    return emptyMessage || 'No CI/CD runs were found for the latest default-branch commit.';\n  }\n  const header = '| Workflow | Status | Conclusion | Run |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |';\n  const rows = list.map(run => {\n    const name = run.name || run.workflowName || 'unknown';\n    const status = run.status || 'unknown';\n    const conclusion = run.conclusion || (status === 'completed' ? 'unknown' : 'in_progress');\n    const url = run.html_url || run.url || '';\n    const runLabel = url ? `[run](${url})` : '—';\n    return `| ${name} | ${status} | ${conclusion} | ${runLabel} |`;\n  });\n  return [header, ...rows].join('\\n');\n}\n\n/** Count the runs that did not pass (failure/cancelled/timed_out/etc.). */\nexport function summarizeRunFailures(runs) {\n  const list = Array.isArray(runs) ? runs : [];\n  const passing = new Set(['success', 'neutral', 'skipped']);\n  const failing = list.filter(run => {\n    const conclusion = (run.conclusion || '').toLowerCase();\n    return run.status === 'completed' && conclusion && !passing.has(conclusion);\n  });\n  return { total: list.length, failing: failing.length };\n}\n\n/**\n * The `/solve` options that `/fix` always turns on. `--development-log`\n * replaces the retired collection paragraph; `--deep-analysis` provides the\n * remaining instructions omitted from the generated issue body (issue #1733).\n */\nexport const SOLVE_OPTION_DEVELOPMENT_LOG = '--development-log';\nexport const SOLVE_OPTION_DEEP_ANALYSIS = '--deep-analysis';\nexport const FIX_FORWARDED_SOLVE_OPTIONS = Object.freeze([SOLVE_OPTION_DEVELOPMENT_LOG, SOLVE_OPTION_DEEP_ANALYSIS]);\n\n/**\n * Paragraphs of the standard prompt, quoted from\n * https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/139.\n *\n * `providedBy` lists the `/solve` options that already inject an equivalent\n * instruction into the AI prompt (see `buildDeepAnalysisPrompt`). A paragraph\n * is dropped from the issue body when every option that provides it is passed\n * to `/solve`.\n *\n * The deep-analysis wording below is the \"bug\" variant, which `/solve` emits\n * only when the issue type is Bug — `/fix` therefore creates the issue with\n * that type (see CI_CD_ISSUE_TYPE).\n *\n * The old case-study instruction from the upstream template is intentionally\n * not represented here. `--development-log` is its replacement; generated\n * issues must never offer or restore the superseded folder convention, even\n * when callers request an otherwise unabridged prompt (PR #1929 feedback).\n */\nexport const DEBUG_OUTPUT_PARAGRAPH = 'If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.';\nexport const REPORT_UPSTREAM_PARAGRAPH = 'If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. i < args.length; i++) {\n    if (args[i] === '--model' || args[i] === '-m') {\n      if (i + 1 < args.length) {\n        const modelName = args[i + 1];\n        const validation = validateModelName(modelName, tool);\n        if (!validation.valid) {\n          return validation.message;\n        }\n      }\n    } else if (args[i].startsWith('--model=')) {\n      const modelName = args[i].substring('--model='.length);\n      const validation = validateModelName(modelName, tool);\n      if (!validation.valid) {\n        return validation.message;\n      }\n    } else if (args[i] === '--sub-agent-model' || args[i].startsWith('--sub-agent-model=')) {\n      const modelName = args[i] === '--sub-agent-model' ? args[i + 1] : args[i].substring('--sub-agent-model='.length);\n      if (!modelName) continue;\n      if (tool !== 'claude') return `--sub-agent-model is only supported with --tool claude (current tool: ${tool})`;\n      const validation = validateClaudeSubAgentModelName(modelName);\n      if (!validation.valid) return `Invalid --sub-agent-model: ${validation.message}`;\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction mergeArgsWithOverrides(userArgs, overrides) {\n  if (!overrides || overrides.length === 0) {\n    return userArgs;\n  }\n\n  // Parse overrides to identify flags and their values\n  const overrideFlags = new Map(); // Map of flag -> value (or null for boolean flags)\n\n  for (let i = 0; i < overrides.length; i++) {\n    const arg = overrides[i];\n    if (arg.startsWith('--')) {\n      // Check if next item is a value (doesn't start with --)\n      if (i + 1 < overrides.length && !overrides[i + 1].startsWith('--')) {\n        overrideFlags.set(arg, overrides[i + 1]);\n        i++; // Skip the value in next iteration\n      } else {\n        overrideFlags.set(arg, null); // Boolean flag\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Filter user args to remove any that conflict with overrides\n  const filteredArgs = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < userArgs.length; i++) {\n    const arg = userArgs[i];\n    if (arg.startsWith('--')) {\n      // If this flag exists in overrides, skip it and its value\n      if (overrideFlags.has(arg)) {\n        // Skip the flag\n        // Also skip next arg if it's a value (doesn't start with --)\n        if (i + 1 < userArgs.length && !userArgs[i + 1].startsWith('--')) {\n          i++; // Skip the value too\n        }\n        continue;\n      }\n    }\n    filteredArgs.push(arg);\n  }\n\n  // Merge: filtered user args + overrides\n  return [...filteredArgs, ...overrides];\n}\n\n// Inject --language LOCALE into spawn args if no language flag is already present.\n// Issue #378: telegram bot resolves the user's effective locale and propagates\n// it to spawned solve/hive sessions so the AI tool replies in the same language.\nfunction injectLanguageIfMissing(args, locale) {\n  if (!locale || !args || !Array.isArray(args)) return args;\n  const langFlags = new Set(['--language', '--ui-language', '--work-language']);\n  for (const arg of args) {\n    const flag = arg.startsWith('--') ? arg.split('=')[0] : null;\n    if (flag && langFlags.has(flag)) return args;\n  }\n  return [...args, '--language', locale];\n}\n\n/** Validate GitHub URL for Telegram bot commands. // Skip the value in next iteration\n      } else {\n        overrideFlags.set(arg, null); // Boolean flag\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Filter user args to remove any that conflict with overrides\n  const filteredArgs = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < userArgs.length; i++) {\n    const arg = userArgs[i];\n    if (arg.startsWith('--')) {\n      // If this flag exists in overrides, skip it and its value\n      if (overrideFlags.has(arg)) {\n        // Skip the flag\n        // Also skip next arg if it's a value (doesn't start with --)\n        if (i + 1 < userArgs.length && !userArgs[i + 1].startsWith('--')) {\n          i++; // Skip the value too\n        }\n        continue;\n      }\n    }\n    filteredArgs.push(arg);\n  }\n\n  // Merge: filtered user args + overrides\n  return [...filteredArgs, ...overrides];\n}\n\n// Inject --language LOCALE into spawn args if no language flag is already present.\n// Issue #378: telegram bot resolves the user's effective locale and propagates\n// it to spawned solve/hive sessions so the AI tool replies in the same language.\nfunction injectLanguageIfMissing(args, locale) {\n  if (!locale || !args || !Array.isArray(args)) return args;\n  const langFlags = new Set(['--language', '--ui-language', '--work-language']);\n  for (const arg of args) {\n    const flag = arg.startsWith('--') ? arg.split('=')[0] : null;\n    if (flag && langFlags.has(flag)) return args;\n  }\n  return [...args, '--language', locale];\n}\n\n/** Validate GitHub URL for Telegram bot commands. 'pull request' : t)).join(', ');\n    const baseUrl = `https://github.com/${parsed.owner}/${parsed.repo}`;\n    const escapedUrl = escapeMarkdown(url),\n      escapedBaseUrl = escapeMarkdown(baseUrl); 'repo') error = t('telegram.url_repo_error', { allowedTypes: allowedTypesStr, url: escapedUrl, example: `${escapedBaseUrl}/issues/1` }, { locale });\n    else error = t('telegram.url_must_be_type', { allowedTypes: allowedTypesStr, type: parsed.type.replace('_', ' ') }, { locale });\n    return { valid: false, error };\n  }\n  return { valid: true, parsed, normalizedUrl: url };\n}\n\nconst i < args.length; i++) {\n    if (args[i] === '--model' || args[i] === '-m') {\n      if (i + 1 < args.length) {\n        const modelName = args[i + 1];\n        const validation = validateModelName(modelName, tool);\n        if (!validation.valid) {\n          return validation.message;\n        }\n      }\n    } else if (args[i].startsWith('--model=')) {\n      const modelName = args[i].substring('--model='.length);\n      const validation = validateModelName(modelName, tool);\n      if (!validation.valid) {\n        return validation.message;\n      }\n    } else if (args[i] === '--sub-agent-model' || args[i].startsWith('--sub-agent-model=')) {\n      const modelName = args[i] === '--sub-agent-model' ? args[i + 1] : args[i].substring('--sub-agent-model='.length);\n      if (!modelName) continue;\n      if (tool !== 'claude') return `--sub-agent-model is only supported with --tool claude (current tool: ${tool})`;\n      const validation = validateClaudeSubAgentModelName(modelName);\n      if (!validation.valid) return `Invalid --sub-agent-model: ${validation.message}`;\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction mergeArgsWithOverrides(userArgs, overrides) {\n  if (!overrides || overrides.length === 0) {\n    return userArgs;\n  }\n\n  // Parse overrides to identify flags and their values\n  const overrideFlags = new Map(); // Map of flag -> value (or null for boolean flags)\n\n  for (let i = 0; i < overrides.length; i++) {\n    const arg = overrides[i];\n    if (arg.startsWith('--')) {\n      // Check if next item is a value (doesn't start with --)\n      if (i + 1 < overrides.length && !overrides[i + 1].startsWith('--')) {\n        overrideFlags.set(arg, overrides[i + 1]);\n        i++; // Skip the value in next iteration\n      } else {\n        overrideFlags.set(arg, null); // Boolean flag\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Filter user args to remove any that conflict with overrides\n  const filteredArgs = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < userArgs.length; i++) {\n    const arg = userArgs[i];\n    if (arg.startsWith('--')) {\n      // If this flag exists in overrides, skip it and its value\n      if (overrideFlags.has(arg)) {\n        // Skip the flag\n        // Also skip next arg if it's a value (doesn't start with --)\n        if (i + 1 < userArgs.length && !userArgs[i + 1].startsWith('--')) {\n          i++; // Skip the value too\n        }\n        continue;\n      }\n    }\n    filteredArgs.push(arg);\n  }\n\n  // Merge: filtered user args + overrides\n  return [...filteredArgs, ...overrides];\n}\n\n// Inject --language LOCALE into spawn args if no language flag is already present.\n// Issue #378: telegram bot resolves the user's effective locale and propagates\n// it to spawned solve/hive sessions so the AI tool replies in the same language.\nfunction injectLanguageIfMissing(args, locale) {\n  if (!locale || !args || !Array.isArray(args)) return args;\n  const langFlags = new Set(['--language', '--ui-language', '--work-language']);\n  for (const arg of args) {\n    const flag = arg.startsWith('--') ? arg.split('=')[0] : null;\n    if (flag && langFlags.has(flag)) return args;\n  }\n  return [...args, '--language', locale];\n}\n\n/** Validate GitHub URL for Telegram bot commands. i < args.length; i++) {\n    if (args[i] === '--model' || args[i] === '-m') {\n      if (i + 1 < args.length) {\n        const modelName = args[i + 1];\n        const validation = validateModelName(modelName, tool);\n        if (!validation.valid) {\n          return validation.message;\n        }\n      }\n    } else if (args[i].startsWith('--model=')) {\n      const modelName = args[i].substring('--model='.length);\n      const validation = validateModelName(modelName, tool);\n      if (!validation.valid) {\n        return validation.message;\n      }\n    } else if (args[i] === '--sub-agent-model' || args[i].startsWith('--sub-agent-model=')) {\n      const modelName = args[i] === '--sub-agent-model' ? args[i + 1] : args[i].substring('--sub-agent-model='.length);\n      if (!modelName) continue;\n      if (tool !== 'claude') return `--sub-agent-model is only supported with --tool claude (current tool: ${tool})`;\n      const validation = validateClaudeSubAgentModelName(modelName);\n      if (!validation.valid) return `Invalid --sub-agent-model: ${validation.message}`;\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction mergeArgsWithOverrides(userArgs, overrides) {\n  if (!overrides || overrides.length === 0) {\n    return userArgs;\n  }\n\n  // Parse overrides to identify flags and their values\n  const overrideFlags = new Map(); // Map of flag -> value (or null for boolean flags)\n\n  for (let i = 0; i < overrides.length; i++) {\n    const arg = overrides[i];\n    if (arg.startsWith('--')) {\n      // Check if next item is a value (doesn't start with --)\n      if (i + 1 < overrides.length && !overrides[i + 1].startsWith('--')) {\n        overrideFlags.set(arg, overrides[i + 1]);\n        i++; // Skip the value in next iteration\n      } else {\n        overrideFlags.set(arg, null); // Boolean flag\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Filter user args to remove any that conflict with overrides\n  const filteredArgs = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < userArgs.length; i++) {\n    const arg = userArgs[i];\n    if (arg.startsWith('--')) {\n      // If this flag exists in overrides, skip it and its value\n      if (overrideFlags.has(arg)) {\n        // Skip the flag\n        // Also skip next arg if it's a value (doesn't start with --)\n        if (i + 1 < userArgs.length && !userArgs[i + 1].startsWith('--')) {\n          i++; // Skip the value too\n        }\n        continue;\n      }\n    }\n    filteredArgs.push(arg);\n  }\n\n  // Merge: filtered user args + overrides\n  return [...filteredArgs, ...overrides];\n}\n\n// Inject --language LOCALE into spawn args if no language flag is already present.\n// Issue #378: telegram bot resolves the user's effective locale and propagates\n// it to spawned solve/hive sessions so the AI tool replies in the same language.\nfunction injectLanguageIfMissing(args, locale) {\n  if (!locale || !args || !Array.isArray(args)) return args;\n  const langFlags = new Set(['--language', '--ui-language', '--work-language']);\n  for (const arg of args) {\n    const flag = arg.startsWith('--') ? arg.split('=')[0] : null;\n    if (flag && langFlags.has(flag)) return args;\n  }\n  return [...args, '--language', locale];\n}\n\n/** Validate GitHub URL for Telegram bot commands. 'pull request' : t)).join(', ');\n    const baseUrl = `https://github.com/${parsed.owner}/${parsed.repo}`;\n    const escapedUrl = escapeMarkdown(url),\n      escapedBaseUrl = escapeMarkdown(baseUrl); // Issue #1102: escape for Markdown\n    let error;\n    if (parsed.type === 'issues_list') error = t('telegram.url_issues_list_error', { url: escapedUrl, example: `${escapedBaseUrl}/issues/1` }, { null : validation.message;\n}\n\nexport function buildFixCommandArgs(text) {\n  const args = applyFixCommandDefaults(parseCommandArgs(text));\n  const repositoryRaw = findFixRepositoryArg(args);\n  const repository = repositoryRaw ? parseFixRepository(repositoryRaw) : null;\n  return {\n    // `fix` reads the repository from the first bare argument, so normalize the\n    // shorthand (`owner/repo`) to a full URL and move it to the front.\n    args: repository ? moveArgumentToFront(args, repository.url, value => parseFixRepository(value)?.url || value) : args,\n    repositoryRaw,\n    repository,\n  };\n}\n\n// Issue #378: inject --language LOCALE into spawn args if no language flag is\n// already present, so spawned fix sessions inherit the user's effective locale.\nfunction injectLanguageIfMissing(args, locale) {\n  if (!locale || !args || !Array.isArray(args)) return args;\n  const langFlags = new Set(['--language', '--ui-language', '--work-language']);\n  for (const arg of args) {\n    const flag = arg.startsWith('--') ? arg.split('=')[0] : null;\n    if (flag && langFlags.has(flag)) return args;\n  }\n  return [...args, '--language', locale];\n}\n\nexport function registerFixCommand(bot, options) {\n  const { VERBOSE, fixEnabled, addBreadcrumb, isOldMessage, isForwardedOrReply, isGroupChat, isTopicAuthorized, buildAuthErrorMessage, isChatStopped, getStoppedChatRejectMessage, safeReply, executeAndUpdateMessage, resolveLocale = null } = options;\n\n  async function handleFixCommand(ctx) {\n    const commandDisplay = '/fix';\n    VERBOSE && console.log(`[VERBOSE] ${commandDisplay} command received`);\n\n    await addBreadcrumb({\n      category: 'telegram.command',\n      message: `${commandDisplay} command received`,\n      level: 'info',\n      data: { chatId: ctx.chat?.id, chatType: ctx.chat?.type, userId: ctx.from?.id, username: ctx.from?.username },\n    });\n\n    if (!fixEnabled) {\n      await ctx.reply('❌ The fix command is disabled on this bot instance.');\n      return;\n    }\n    if (isOldMessage(ctx)) return;\n    // Issue #1922: a forwarded or replied-to /fix command must never be\n    // re-executed. Unlike /task, /fix takes no input from the replied message,\n    // so both cases are ignored.\n    if (isForwardedOrReply && isForwardedOrReply(ctx)) {\n      VERBOSE && console.log(`[VERBOSE] ${commandDisplay} ignored: forwarded or reply message`);\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!isGroupChat(ctx)) {\n      await ctx.reply(`❌ The ${commandDisplay} command only works in group chats. Please add this bot to a group and make it an admin.`, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!isTopicAuthorized(ctx)) {\n      await ctx.reply(buildAuthErrorMessage(ctx), { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n    if (isChatStopped(ctx.chat.id)) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, getStoppedChatRejectMessage(ctx.chat.id, 'Fix'), { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const built = buildFixCommandArgs(ctx.message.text);\n    if (!built.repository) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, `❌ Missing GitHub repository URL. Usage: \\`${commandDisplay} <github-repository-url> [options]\\`\\n\\nExample: \\`${commandDisplay} https://github.com/owner/repo\\``, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const { backend: perCommandIsolation, filteredArgs } = extractIsolationFromArgs(built.args);\n    if (perCommandIsolation && !isValidPerCommandIsolation(perCommandIsolation)) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, `❌ Invalid --isolation value '${escapeMarkdown(perCommandIsolation)}'. Must be: screen, tmux, or docker`, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const modelError = validateFixModel(filteredArgs);\n    if (modelError) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, `❌ ${escapeMarkdown(modelError)}`, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const requester = buildUserMention({ user: ctx.from, parseMode: 'Markdown' });\n    const userOptionsRaw = built.args.slice(1).join(' ');\n    let infoBlock = `Requested by: ${requester}\\nRepository: ${escapeMarkdown(built.repository.url)}`;\n    if (userOptionsRaw) infoBlock += `\\n\\n🛠 Options: ${escapeMarkdown(userOptionsRaw)}`;\n\n    const fixUrlContext = { owner: built.repository.owner, repo: built.repository.repo, normalized: built.repository.url };\n    const startingMessage = await safeReply(ctx, formatStartingWorkSessionMessage({ infoBlock }), { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n    const fixLocale = resolveLocale ? resolveLocale(ctx) : null;\n    const argsForExec = injectLanguageIfMissing(filteredArgs, fixLocale);\n    await executeAndUpdateMessage(ctx, startingMessage, 'fix', argsForExec, infoBlock, perCommandIsolation || null, getFixToolFromArgs(argsForExec), fixUrlContext);\n  }\n\n  bot.command(\n    FIX_COMMAND_NAMES.map(command => new RegExp(`^${command}$`, 'i')),\n    handleFixCommand\n  );\n\n  return { handleFixCommand, FIX_COMMAND_NAMES };\n}\n",

[2026-07-19T23:50:22.206Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "/**\n * Telegram `/fix` command (issue #1733).\n *\n * Spawns the `fix` CLI in a work session, exactly like `/solve` and `/task` do\n * for their own CLIs. `fix` creates the CI/CD remediation issue and then hands\n * it off to `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge` itself, so\n * this handler only has to validate the request and start the session.\n */\n\nimport { buildUserMention } from './buildUserMention.lib.mjs';\nimport { validateModelName } from './models/index.mjs';\nimport { parseFixRepository } from './fix.ci-cd.lib.mjs';\nimport { escapeMarkdown } from './telegram-markdown.lib.mjs';\nimport { extractIsolationFromArgs, isValidPerCommandIsolation } from './telegram-isolation.lib.mjs';\nimport { mergeArgsWithOverrides } from './args-overrides.lib.mjs';\nimport { moveArgumentToFront, parseCommandArgs } from './telegram-solve-command.lib.mjs';\nimport { formatStartingWorkSessionMessage } from './work-session-formatting.lib.mjs';\n\nexport const FIX_COMMAND_NAMES = Object.freeze(['fix']);\n\nexport function getFixCommandNameFromText(text) {\n  if (!text || typeof text !== 'string') return null;\n  const firstLine = text.split('\\n')[0].trim();\n  const match = firstLine.match(/^\\/(\\w+)(?:@\\S+)?(?:\\s|$)/);\n  const command = match ? match[1].toLowerCase() : null;\n  return FIX_COMMAND_NAMES.includes(command) ? command : null;\n}\n\n/**\n * `--ci-cd` is the only mode `fix` supports today and it is required by the\n * CLI, so the chat command implies it instead of making every user type it.\n */\nexport function applyFixCommandDefaults(args) {\n  const hasCiCd = args.includes('--ci-cd');\n  return hasCiCd ? args : [...args, '--ci-cd'];\n}\n\nexport function findFixRepositoryArg(args) {\n  return args.find(arg => !arg.startsWith('-') && parseFixRepository(arg)) || null;\n}\n\nexport function getFixToolFromArgs(args) {\n  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {\n    if (args[i] === '--tool' && i + 1 < args.length) return args[i + 1];\n    if (args[i].startsWith('--tool=')) return args[i].substring('--tool='.length);\n  }\n  return 'claude';\n}\n\nfunction getModelFromArgs(args) {\n  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {\n    if ((args[i] === '--model' || args[i] === '-m') && i + 1 < args.length) return args[i + 1];\n    if (args[i].startsWith('--model=')) return args[i].substring('--model='.length);\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction validateFixModel(args) {\n  const model = getModelFromArgs(args);\n  if (!model) return null;\n  const validation = validateModelName(model, getFixToolFromArgs(args));\n  return validation.valid ? null : validation.message;\n}\n\nexport function buildFixCommandArgs(text) {\n  const args = applyFixCommandDefaults(parseCommandArgs(text));\n  const repositoryRaw = findFixRepositoryArg(args);\n  const repository = repositoryRaw ? parseFixRepository(repositoryRaw) : null;\n  return {\n    // `fix` reads the repository from the first bare argument, so normalize the\n    // shorthand (`owner/repo`) to a full URL and move it to the front.\n    args: repository ? moveArgumentToFront(args, repository.url, value => parseFixRepository(value)?.url || value) : args,\n    repositoryRaw,\n    repository,\n  };\n}\n\n// Issue #378: inject --language LOCALE into spawn args if no language flag is\n// already present, so spawned fix sessions inherit the user's effective locale.\nfunction injectLanguageIfMissing(args, locale) {\n  if (!locale || !args || !Array.isArray(args)) return args;\n  const langFlags = new Set(['--language', '--ui-language', '--work-language']);\n  for (const arg of args) {\n    const flag = arg.startsWith('--') ? arg.split('=')[0] : null;\n    if (flag && langFlags.has(flag)) return args;\n  }\n  return [...args, '--language', locale];\n}\n\nexport function registerFixCommand(bot, options) {\n  const { VERBOSE, fixEnabled, addBreadcrumb, isOldMessage, isForwardedOrReply, isGroupChat, isTopicAuthorized, buildAuthErrorMessage, isChatStopped, getStoppedChatRejectMessage, safeReply, executeAndUpdateMessage, resolveLocale = null } = options;\n\n  async function handleFixCommand(ctx) {\n    const commandDisplay = '/fix';\n    VERBOSE && console.log(`[VERBOSE] ${commandDisplay} command received`);\n\n    await addBreadcrumb({\n      category: 'telegram.command',\n      message: `${commandDisplay} command received`,\n      level: 'info',\n      data: { chatId: ctx.chat?.id, chatType: ctx.chat?.type, userId: ctx.from?.id, username: ctx.from?.username },\n    });\n\n    if (!fixEnabled) {\n      await ctx.reply('❌ The fix command is disabled on this bot instance.');\n      return;\n    }\n    if (isOldMessage(ctx)) return;\n    // Issue #1922: a forwarded or replied-to /fix command must never be\n    // re-executed. Unlike /task, /fix takes no input from the replied message,\n    // so both cases are ignored.\n    if (isForwardedOrReply && isForwardedOrReply(ctx)) {\n      VERBOSE && console.log(`[VERBOSE] ${commandDisplay} ignored: forwarded or reply message`);\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!isGroupChat(ctx)) {\n      await ctx.reply(`❌ The ${commandDisplay} command only works in group chats. Please add this bot to a group and make it an admin.`, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!isTopicAuthorized(ctx)) {\n      await ctx.reply(buildAuthErrorMessage(ctx), { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n    if (isChatStopped(ctx.chat.id)) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, getStoppedChatRejectMessage(ctx.chat.id, 'Fix'), { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const built = buildFixCommandArgs(ctx.message.text);\n    if (!built.repository) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, `❌ Missing GitHub repository URL. Usage: \\`${commandDisplay} <github-repository-url> [options]\\`\\n\\nExample: \\`${commandDisplay} https://github.com/owner/repo\\``, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const { backend: perCommandIsolation, filteredArgs } = extractIsolationFromArgs(built.args);\n    if (perCommandIsolation && !isValidPerCommandIsolation(perCommandIsolation)) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, `❌ Invalid --isolation value '${escapeMarkdown(perCommandIsolation)}'. Must be: screen, tmux, or docker`, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const modelError = validateFixModel(filteredArgs);\n    if (modelError) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, `❌ ${escapeMarkdown(modelError)}`, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const requester = buildUserMention({ user: ctx.from, parseMode: 'Markdown' });\n    const userOptionsRaw = built.args.slice(1).join(' ');\n    let infoBlock = `Requested by: ${requester}\\nRepository: ${escapeMarkdown(built.repository.url)}`;\n    if (userOptionsRaw) infoBlock += `\\n\\n🛠 Options: ${escapeMarkdown(userOptionsRaw)}`;\n\n    const fixUrlContext = { owner: built.repository.owner, repo: built.repository.repo, normalized: built.repository.url };\n    const startingMessage = await safeReply(ctx, formatStartingWorkSessionMessage({ infoBlock }), { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n    const fixLocale = resolveLocale ? resolveLocale(ctx) : null;\n    const argsForExec = injectLanguageIfMissing(filteredArgs, fixLocale);\n    await executeAndUpdateMessage(ctx, startingMessage, 'fix', argsForExec, infoBlock, perCommandIsolation || null, getFixToolFromArgs(argsForExec), fixUrlContext);\n  }\n\n  bot.command(\n    FIX_COMMAND_NAMES.map(command => new RegExp(`^${command}$`, 'i')),\n    handleFixCommand\n  );\n\n  return { handleFixCommand, FIX_COMMAND_NAMES };\n}\n",

match[1].toLowerCase() : null;\n  return FIX_COMMAND_NAMES.includes(command) ? command : null;\n}\n\n/**\n * `--ci-cd` is the only mode `fix` supports today and it is required by the\n * CLI, so the chat command implies it instead of making every user type it.\n */\nexport function applyFixCommandDefaults(args) {\n  const hasCiCd = args.includes('--ci-cd');\n  return hasCiCd ? args : [...args, '--ci-cd'];\n}\n\nexport function findFixRepositoryArg(args) {\n  return args.find(arg => !arg.startsWith('-') && parseFixRepository(arg)) || null;\n}\n\nexport function getFixToolFromArgs(args) {\n  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {\n    if (args[i] === '--tool' && i + 1 < args.length) return args[i + 1];\n    if (args[i].startsWith('--tool=')) return args[i].substring('--tool='.length);\n  }\n  return 'claude';\n}\n\nfunction getModelFromArgs(args) {\n  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {\n    if ((args[i] === '--model' || args[i] === '-m') && i + 1 < args.length) return args[i + 1];\n    if (args[i].startsWith('--model=')) return args[i].substring('--model='.length);\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction validateFixModel(args) {\n  const model = getModelFromArgs(args);\n  if (!model) return null;\n  const validation = validateModelName(model, getFixToolFromArgs(args));\n  return validation.valid ? null : validation.message;\n}\n\nexport function buildFixCommandArgs(text) {\n  const args = applyFixCommandDefaults(parseCommandArgs(text));\n  const repositoryRaw = findFixRepositoryArg(args);\n  const repository = repositoryRaw ? parseFixRepository(repositoryRaw) : null;\n  return {\n    // `fix` reads the repository from the first bare argument, so normalize the\n    // shorthand (`owner/repo`) to a full URL and move it to the front.\n    args: repository ? arg.split('=')[0] : null;\n    if (flag && langFlags.has(flag)) return args;\n  }\n  return [...args, '--language', locale];\n}\n\nexport function registerFixCommand(bot, options) {\n  const { VERBOSE, fixEnabled, addBreadcrumb, isOldMessage, isForwardedOrReply, isGroupChat, isTopicAuthorized, buildAuthErrorMessage, isChatStopped, getStoppedChatRejectMessage, safeReply, executeAndUpdateMessage, resolveLocale = null, solveOverrides = [] } = options;\n\n  async function handleFixCommand(ctx) {\n    const commandDisplay = '/fix';\n    VERBOSE && console.log(`[VERBOSE] ${commandDisplay} command received`);\n\n    await addBreadcrumb({\n      category: 'telegram.command',\n      message: `${commandDisplay} command received`,\n      level: 'info',\n      data: { chatId: ctx.chat?.id, chatType: ctx.chat?.type, userId: ctx.from?.id, username: ctx.from?.username },\n    });\n\n    if (!fixEnabled) {\n      await ctx.reply('❌ The fix command is disabled on this bot instance.');\n      return;\n    }\n    if (isOldMessage(ctx)) return;\n    // Issue #1922: a forwarded or replied-to /fix command must never be\n    // re-executed. Unlike /task, /fix takes no input from the replied message,\n    // so both cases are ignored.\n    if (isForwardedOrReply && isForwardedOrReply(ctx)) {\n      VERBOSE && console.log(`[VERBOSE] ${commandDisplay} ignored: forwarded or reply message`);\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!isGroupChat(ctx)) {\n      await ctx.reply(`❌ The ${commandDisplay} command only works in group chats. Please add this bot to a group and make it an admin.`, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!isTopicAuthorized(ctx)) {\n      await ctx.reply(buildAuthErrorMessage(ctx), { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n    if (isChatStopped(ctx.chat.id)) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, getStoppedChatRejectMessage(ctx.chat.id, 'Fix'), { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const built = buildFixCommandArgs(ctx.message.text);\n    if (!built.repository) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, `❌ Missing GitHub repository URL. Usage: \\`${commandDisplay} <github-repository-url> [options]\\`\\n\\nExample: \\`${commandDisplay} https://github.com/owner/repo\\``, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const { backend: perCommandIsolation, filteredArgs } = extractIsolationFromArgs(built.args);\n    if (perCommandIsolation && !isValidPerCommandIsolation(perCommandIsolation)) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, `❌ Invalid --isolation value '${escapeMarkdown(perCommandIsolation)}'. Must be: screen, tmux, or docker`, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const modelError = validateFixModel(filteredArgs);\n    if (modelError) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, `❌ ${escapeMarkdown(modelError)}`, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const requester = buildUserMention({ user: ctx.from, parseMode: 'Markdown' });\n    const userOptionsRaw = built.args.slice(1).join(' ');\n    let infoBlock = `Requested by: ${requester}\\nRepository: ${escapeMarkdown(built.repository.url)}`;\n    if (userOptionsRaw) infoBlock += `\\n\\n🛠 Options: ${escapeMarkdown(userOptionsRaw)}`;\n\n    const fixUrlContext = { owner: built.repository.owner, repo: built.repository.repo, normalized: built.repository.url };\n    const startingMessage = await safeReply(ctx, formatStartingWorkSessionMessage({ infoBlock }), { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n    const fixLocale = resolveLocale ? resolveLocale(ctx) : null;\n    const argsForExec = injectLanguageIfMissing(filteredArgs, fixLocale);\n    await executeAndUpdateMessage(ctx, startingMessage, 'fix', argsForExec, infoBlock, perCommandIsolation || null, getFixToolFromArgs(argsForExec), fixUrlContext);\n  }\n\n  bot.command(\n    FIX_COMMAND_NAMES.map(command => new RegExp(`^${command}$`, 'i')),\n    handleFixCommand\n  );\n\n  return { handleFixCommand, FIX_COMMAND_NAMES };\n}\n",

    "originalFile": "/**\n * Telegram `/fix` command (issue #1733).\n *\n * Spawns the `fix` CLI in a work session, exactly like `/solve` and `/task` do\n * for their own CLIs. `fix` creates the CI/CD remediation issue and then hands\n * it off to `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge` itself, so\n * this handler only has to validate the request and start the session.\n */\n\nimport { buildUserMention } from './buildUserMention.lib.mjs';\nimport { validateModelName } from './models/index.mjs';\nimport { parseFixRepository } from './fix.ci-cd.lib.mjs';\nimport { escapeMarkdown } from './telegram-markdown.lib.mjs';\nimport { extractIsolationFromArgs, isValidPerCommandIsolation } from './telegram-isolation.lib.mjs';\nimport { mergeArgsWithOverrides } from './args-overrides.lib.mjs';\nimport { moveArgumentToFront, parseCommandArgs } from './telegram-solve-command.lib.mjs';\nimport { formatStartingWorkSessionMessage } from './work-session-formatting.lib.mjs';\n\nexport const FIX_COMMAND_NAMES = Object.freeze(['fix']);\n\nexport function getFixCommandNameFromText(text) {\n  if (!text || typeof text !== 'string') return null;\n  const firstLine = text.split('\\n')[0].trim();\n  const match = firstLine.match(/^\\/(\\w+)(?:@\\S+)?(?:\\s|$)/);\n  const command = match ? match[1].toLowerCase() : null;\n  return FIX_COMMAND_NAMES.includes(command) ? command : null;\n}\n\n/**\n * `--ci-cd` is the only mode `fix` supports today and it is required by the\n * CLI, so the chat command implies it instead of making every user type it.\n */\nexport function applyFixCommandDefaults(args) {\n  const hasCiCd = args.includes('--ci-cd');\n  return hasCiCd ? args : [...args, '--ci-cd'];\n}\n\nexport function findFixRepositoryArg(args) {\n  return args.find(arg => !arg.startsWith('-') && parseFixRepository(arg)) || null;\n}\n\nexport function getFixToolFromArgs(args) {\n  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {\n    if (args[i] === '--tool' && i + 1 < args.length) return args[i + 1];\n    if (args[i].startsWith('--tool=')) return args[i].substring('--tool='.length);\n  }\n  return 'claude';\n}\n\nfunction getModelFromArgs(args) {\n  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {\n    if ((args[i] === '--model' || args[i] === '-m') && i + 1 < args.length) return args[i + 1];\n    if (args[i].startsWith('--model=')) return args[i].substring('--model='.length);\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction validateFixModel(args) {\n  const model = getModelFromArgs(args);\n  if (!model) return null;\n  const validation = validateModelName(model, getFixToolFromArgs(args));\n  return validation.valid ? null : validation.message;\n}\n\nexport function buildFixCommandArgs(text) {\n  const args = applyFixCommandDefaults(parseCommandArgs(text));\n  const repositoryRaw = findFixRepositoryArg(args);\n  const repository = repositoryRaw ? parseFixRepository(repositoryRaw) : null;\n  return {\n    // `fix` reads the repository from the first bare argument, so normalize the\n    // shorthand (`owner/repo`) to a full URL and move it to the front.\n    args: repository ? moveArgumentToFront(args, repository.url, value => parseFixRepository(value)?.url || value) : args,\n    repositoryRaw,\n    repository,\n  };\n}\n\n// Issue #378: inject --language LOCALE into spawn args if no language flag is\n// already present, so spawned fix sessions inherit the user's effective locale.\nfunction injectLanguageIfMissing(args, locale) {\n  if (!locale || !args || !Array.isArray(args)) return args;\n  const langFlags = new Set(['--language', '--ui-language', '--work-language']);\n  for (const arg of args) {\n    const flag = arg.startsWith('--') ? arg.split('=')[0] : null;\n    if (flag && langFlags.has(flag)) return args;\n  }\n  return [...args, '--language', locale];\n}\n\nexport function registerFixCommand(bot, options) {\n  const { VERBOSE, fixEnabled, addBreadcrumb, isOldMessage, isForwardedOrReply, isGroupChat, isTopicAuthorized, buildAuthErrorMessage, isChatStopped, getStoppedChatRejectMessage, safeReply, executeAndUpdateMessage, resolveLocale = null, solveOverrides = [] } = options;\n\n  async function handleFixCommand(ctx) {\n    const commandDisplay = '/fix';\n    VERBOSE && console.log(`[VERBOSE] ${commandDisplay} command received`);\n\n    await addBreadcrumb({\n      category: 'telegram.command',\n      message: `${commandDisplay} command received`,\n      level: 'info',\n      data: { chatId: ctx.chat?.id, chatType: ctx.chat?.type, userId: ctx.from?.id, username: ctx.from?.username },\n    });\n\n    if (!fixEnabled) {\n      await ctx.reply('❌ The fix command is disabled on this bot instance.');\n      return;\n    }\n    if (isOldMessage(ctx)) return;\n    // Issue #1922: a forwarded or replied-to /fix command must never be\n    // re-executed. Unlike /task, /fix takes no input from the replied message,\n    // so both cases are ignored.\n    if (isForwardedOrReply && isForwardedOrReply(ctx)) {\n      VERBOSE && console.log(`[VERBOSE] ${commandDisplay} ignored: forwarded or reply message`);\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!isGroupChat(ctx)) {\n      await ctx.reply(`❌ The ${commandDisplay} command only works in group chats. Please add this bot to a group and make it an admin.`, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n    if (!isTopicAuthorized(ctx)) {\n      await ctx.reply(buildAuthErrorMessage(ctx), { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n    if (isChatStopped(ctx.chat.id)) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, getStoppedChatRejectMessage(ctx.chat.id, 'Fix'), { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const built = buildFixCommandArgs(ctx.message.text);\n    if (!built.repository) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, `❌ Missing GitHub repository URL. Usage: \\`${commandDisplay} <github-repository-url> [options]\\`\\n\\nExample: \\`${commandDisplay} https://github.com/owner/repo\\``, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const { backend: perCommandIsolation, filteredArgs } = extractIsolationFromArgs(built.args);\n    if (perCommandIsolation && !isValidPerCommandIsolation(perCommandIsolation)) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, `❌ Invalid --isolation value '${escapeMarkdown(perCommandIsolation)}'. Must be: screen, tmux, or docker`, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const modelError = validateFixModel(filteredArgs);\n    if (modelError) {\n      await safeReply(ctx, `❌ ${escapeMarkdown(modelError)}`, { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const requester = buildUserMention({ user: ctx.from, parseMode: 'Markdown' });\n    const userOptionsRaw = built.args.slice(1).join(' ');\n    let infoBlock = `Requested by: ${requester}\\nRepository: ${escapeMarkdown(built.repository.url)}`;\n    if (userOptionsRaw) infoBlock += `\\n\\n🛠 Options: ${escapeMarkdown(userOptionsRaw)}`;\n\n    const fixUrlContext = { owner: built.repository.owner, repo: built.repository.repo, normalized: built.repository.url };\n    const startingMessage = await safeReply(ctx, formatStartingWorkSessionMessage({ infoBlock }), { reply_to_message_id: ctx.message.message_id });\n    const fixLocale = resolveLocale ? resolveLocale(ctx) : null;\n    const argsForExec = injectLanguageIfMissing(filteredArgs, fixLocale);\n    await executeAndUpdateMessage(ctx, startingMessage, 'fix', argsForExec, infoBlock, perCommandIsolation || null, getFixToolFromArgs(argsForExec), fixUrlContext);\n  }\n\n  bot.command(\n    FIX_COMMAND_NAMES.map(command => new RegExp(`^${command}$`, 'i')),\n    handleFixCommand\n  );\n\n  return { handleFixCommand, FIX_COMMAND_NAMES };\n}\n",

[2026-07-19T23:59:21.932Z] [INFO]           "content": "# Case study — Issue #2085\n\n> `/fix --ci-cd` does not call real /solve command with working session, that\n> leads to no defaults for the solve command applied\n\n- **Issue:** <https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2085>\n- **Author:** konard\n- **Opened:** 2026-07-19\n- **Working PR:** <https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2087>\n- **Cited run:** <https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2083> (a `/fix --ci-cd` run for issue #2082)\n- **Origin:** <https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1733> (the original `/fix` request)\n\nThe raw data backing this analysis is in [`data/`](./data), the external\nreferences are indexed in [`research-sources.json`](./research-sources.json).\n\n---\n\n## 1. Timeline / sequence of events\n\n1. **#1733** requested that `/fix --ci-cd` behave as a combination of `/task`\n   and `/solve`: generate the CI/CD remediation issue, then run\n   `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge` on it, **passing\n   through all options that `/fix` itself does not consume** (`--tool`,\n   `--model`, `--think`, and ideally everything else).\n2. `/fix` was implemented (`src/fix.mjs`, `src/fix.ci-cd.lib.mjs`) and the\n   Telegram `/fix` command was added (`src/telegram-fix-command.lib.mjs`,\n   issue #1733). The Telegram handler spawns the real `fix` CLI, which in turn\n   spawns the real `solve.mjs`.\n3. **PR #2083** was produced by a real `/fix --ci-cd` run against issue #2082.\n   Its captured solve-session `metadata.json` records the exact command that\n   was launched (see [`data/pr-2083-solve-metadata.json`](./data/pr-2083-solve-metadata.json)):\n\n   ```text\n   node .../src/solve.mjs https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2082 \\\n     --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge --language en\n   ```\n\n4. **#2085** was opened: the operator observed that `--attach-logs` — a solve\n   default they had configured — **was not applied** to the solve started by\n   `/fix`, and asked whether the solve was \"entirely fake.\" The issue restates\n   the #1733 expectation: no fancy re-invention, just `/task` + `/solve`.\n\n## 2. Requirements extracted from the issue\n\n| # | Requirement | Status |\n|---|-------------|--------|\n| R1 | `/fix --ci-cd` must call the **real** `/solve` in a real working session (not a fake/emulated one). | Already true — verified, see §3. |\n| R2 | Solve **defaults/overrides** (e.g. `--attach-logs`) configured for `/solve` must also apply to the solve started by `/fix`. | **Fixed** in this PR. |\n| R3 | Behave as a straightforward combination of `/task` + `/solve` as originally asked in #1733 — no fancy re-invention. | Satisfied — fix reuses the exact same override mechanism `/solve` uses. |\n| R4 | Download all logs/data about the issue into `docs/case-studies/issue-2085/`. | Done — this folder. |\n| R5 | Deep case study: timeline, requirements, root causes, solution plans, existing-components review. | This document. |\n| R6 | Search online for additional facts/data. | Done — see [`research-sources.json`](./research-sources.json). |\n| R7 | If root cause is unclear, add debug/verbose output for the next iteration. | Root cause was determinable from PR #2083's metadata; no new tracing required. Existing `--verbose` already surfaces the merged args. |\n| R8 | If another repo is involved, report there with reproducible examples. | Not applicable — the defect is entirely within this repo (Telegram bot wiring). No external project involved. |\n| R9 | Fix in **all** places the bug exists across the codebase. | Audited — see §5. Only the `/fix` Telegram handler was affected; `/solve` and `/hive` already applied overrides. |\n| R10 | Do everything in the single PR #2087; add tests; prepare a release (version/changeset); CI green. | In progress in this PR. |\n\n## 3. Root-cause analysis\n\n### R1 — Is the solve \"fake\"? No.\n\n`src/fix.mjs` spawns the real `solve.mjs` with `stdio: 'inherit'` via\n`buildSolveArgs()` in `src/fix.ci-cd.lib.mjs`, producing\n`[issueUrl, --development-log, --deep-analysis, --auto-merge, ...passthrough]`.\nPR #2083's `metadata.json` `rawCommand` field is the primary evidence: it shows\na genuine `node .../src/solve.mjs …` invocation. **The solve is real.** The\n\"fake\" hypothesis in the issue title is disproved by the captured data.\n\n### R2 — Why `--attach-logs` was missing (the actual bug)\n\nOperators configure solve defaults through the **`TELEGRAM_SOLVE_OVERRIDES`**\nenvironment variable (lino-formatted, e.g. `(\\n  --attach-logs\\n  --auto-continue\\n)`).\nThe Telegram bot parses this into a `solveOverrides` array\n(`src/telegram-bot.mjs`) and merges it into user args via\n`mergeArgsWithOverrides()` — but **only for the `/solve` and `/hive` handlers**.\n\nThe `/fix` handler (`src/telegram-fix-command.lib.mjs`) never received\n`solveOverrides` and never merged them. So when `/fix` forwarded its arguments\nto the real `solve.mjs`, the operator overrides were absent — exactly why\n`--attach-logs` did not appear in PR #2083's `rawCommand`.\n\nThis is a **wiring gap**, not a solve defect: `/fix` genuinely delegates to\n`/solve`, but the operator-default layer that sits *in front of* `/solve` in the\nTelegram bot was not applied to the `/fix` delegation.\n\nWhy the override must be baked into the **arguments** (not read from env by\n`fix.mjs`): the bot runs work sessions under isolation backends\n(screen/tmux/**docker**). `buildDockerIsolationStartArgs()` only forwards\nexplicitly listed `-e` environment variables into the container, so a Docker\n`/fix` session would not see `TELEGRAM_SOLVE_OVERRIDES` at all. Applying the\noverrides at the Telegram handler (baking them into the forwarded args) is the\nonly approach that is robust across every isolation backend — and it is exactly\nwhat the `/solve` handler already does.\n\n## 4. Solution (implemented in PR #2087)\n\n1. **Extract the shared helper.** `mergeArgsWithOverrides()` was moved out of\n   `src/telegram-bot.mjs` into a new shared module\n   [`src/args-overrides.lib.mjs`](../../../src/args-overrides.lib.mjs) (with\n   added `Array.isArray` null-safety) so `/solve`, `/hive` **and** `/fix` share\n   one implementation — no copy/paste, no circular import on the bot entry\n   point.\n2. **Wire overrides into `/fix`.** `registerFixCommand()` now accepts\n   `solveOverrides`, and `handleFixCommand()`:\n   - extracts any `--isolation` from the overrides\n     (`extractIsolationFromArgs`), validates it, and lets an override isolation\n     take precedence over a per-command one (`effectiveIsolation`);\n   - merges the remaining overrides into the fix args with\n     `mergeArgsWithOverrides()` (overrides win, appended last for yargs'\n     last-wins parsing);\n   - validates the model on the *merged* args;\n   - surfaces a `🔒 Solve overrides: …` line in the work-session info block so\n     the operator can see the locked options.\n3. **Telegram bot passes `solveOverrides` to `registerFixCommand`.**\n\nBecause `/fix` forwards every option it does not consume through to\n`solve.mjs`, appending the solve overrides to the fix args makes them reach the\nreal solve invocation — restoring `--attach-logs` and any other operator\ndefault.\n\n### Why this matches #1733's \"no fancy re-invention\"\n\nThe fix does **not** add a new mechanism. It reuses the *identical* override\nmerge that `/solve` already uses, so `/fix`'s embedded solve is now configured\nexactly like a direct `/solve` — the combination of `/task` + `/solve` that\n#1733 asked for.\n\n## 5. Codebase audit — is the bug anywhere else?\n\n- `/solve` handler — already merges `solveOverrides`. ✅\n- `/hive` handler — already merges `hiveOverrides`. ✅\n- `/fix` handler — **was missing**; fixed here. ✅\n- `/task` handler — does not delegate to `/solve`, so no solve overrides apply. ✅\n- Direct CLI `fix` (outside Telegram) — `TELEGRAM_SOLVE_OVERRIDES` is a\n  Telegram-bot concept; the direct CLI already forwards user options to\n  `solve.mjs`. No change needed. ✅\n\nNo other delegation site omits the overrides.\n\n## 6. Existing components / libraries reviewed\n\n- **`mergeArgsWithOverrides` (internal, issue #1228).** The repo already had a\n  battle-tested override-merge helper for `/solve` and `/hive`. Rather than\n  writing something new, this fix promotes it to a shared module and reuses it.\n  This is the \"known existing component that solves a similar problem.\"\n- **yargs last-wins parsing** ([advanced docs](https://github.com/yargs/yargs/blob/main/docs/advanced.md)).\n  `solve.mjs`/`fix.mjs` parse with yargs, where the last occurrence of an option\n  wins. Appending overrides at the end of the arg list is therefore the correct,\n  documented way to guarantee they take precedence — matching the existing\n  helper's contract.\n- **`extractIsolationFromArgs` / `isValidPerCommandIsolation`** (internal). Reused\n  verbatim to handle an `--isolation` override consistently with `/solve`.\n\n## 7. Tests added\n\n- [`tests/test-args-overrides.mjs`](../../../tests/test-args-overrides.mjs) —\n  unit tests for the extracted `mergeArgsWithOverrides` (imports the real\n  module, not a replica).\n- [`tests/test-telegram-fix-command.mjs`](../../../tests/test-telegram-fix-command.mjs) —\n  new cases proving `/fix` applies solve overrides, that overrides win over a\n  conflicting user flag, that an `--isolation` override is honored, that a\n  per-command `--isolation` still applies, that an invalid override isolation is\n  rejected, and that the info block shows/omits the locked-options line.\n"

No.\n\n`src/fix.mjs` spawns the real `solve.mjs` with `stdio: 'inherit'` via\n`buildSolveArgs()` in `src/fix.ci-cd.lib.mjs`, producing\n`[issueUrl, --development-log, --deep-analysis, --auto-merge, ...passthrough]`.\nPR #2083's `metadata.json` `rawCommand` field is the primary evidence: it shows\na genuine `node .../src/solve.mjs …` invocation. **The solve is real.** The\n\"fake\" hypothesis in the issue title is disproved by the captured data.\n\n### R2 — Why `--attach-logs` was missing (the actual bug)\n\nOperators configure solve defaults through the **`TELEGRAM_SOLVE_OVERRIDES`**\nenvironment variable (lino-formatted, e.g. `(\\n  --attach-logs\\n  --auto-continue\\n)`).\nThe Telegram bot parses this into a `solveOverrides` array\n(`src/telegram-bot.mjs`) and merges it into user args via\n`mergeArgsWithOverrides()` — but **only for the `/solve` and `/hive` handlers**.\n\nThe `/fix` handler (`src/telegram-fix-command.lib.mjs`) never received\n`solveOverrides` and never merged them. So when `/fix` forwarded its arguments\nto the real `solve.mjs`, the operator overrides were absent — exactly why\n`--attach-logs` did not appear in PR #2083's `rawCommand`.\n\nThis is a **wiring gap**, not a solve defect: `/fix` genuinely delegates to\n`/solve`, but the operator-default layer that sits *in front of* `/solve` in the\nTelegram bot was not applied to the `/fix` delegation.\n\nWhy the override must be baked into the **arguments** (not read from env by\n`fix.mjs`): the bot runs work sessions under isolation backends\n(screen/tmux/**docker**). `buildDockerIsolationStartArgs()` only forwards\nexplicitly listed `-e` environment variables into the container, so a Docker\n`/fix` session would not see `TELEGRAM_SOLVE_OVERRIDES` at all. Applying the\noverrides at the Telegram handler (baking them into the forwarded args) is the\nonly approach that is robust across every isolation backend — and it is exactly\nwhat the `/solve` handler already does.\n\n## 4. Solution (implemented in PR #2087)\n\n1. **Extract the shared helper.** `mergeArgsWithOverrides()` was moved out of\n   `src/telegram-bot.mjs` into a new shared module\n   [`src/args-overrides.lib.mjs`](../../../src/args-overrides.lib.mjs) (with\n   added `Array.isArray` null-safety) so `/solve`, `/hive` **and** `/fix` share\n   one implementation — no copy/paste, no circular import on the bot entry\n   point.\n2. **Wire overrides into `/fix`.** `registerFixCommand()` now accepts\n   `solveOverrides`, and `handleFixCommand()`:\n   - extracts any `--isolation` from the overrides\n     (`extractIsolationFromArgs`), validates it, and lets an override isolation\n     take precedence over a per-command one (`effectiveIsolation`);\n   - merges the remaining overrides into the fix args with\n     `mergeArgsWithOverrides()` (overrides win, appended last for yargs'\n     last-wins parsing);\n   - validates the model on the *merged* args;\n   - surfaces a `🔒 Solve overrides: …` line in the work-session info block so\n     the operator can see the locked options.\n3. **Telegram bot passes `solveOverrides` to `registerFixCommand`.**\n\nBecause `/fix` forwards every option it does not consume through to\n`solve.mjs`, appending the solve overrides to the fix args makes them reach the\nreal solve invocation — restoring `--attach-logs` and any other operator\ndefault.\n\n### Why this matches #1733's \"no fancy re-invention\"\n\nThe fix does **not** add a new mechanism. It reuses the *identical* override\nmerge that `/solve` already uses, so `/fix`'s embedded solve is now configured\nexactly like a direct `/solve` — the combination of `/task` + `/solve` that\n#1733 asked for.\n\n## 5. Codebase audit — is the bug anywhere else?\n\n- `/solve` handler — already merges `solveOverrides`. ✅\n- `/hive` handler — already merges `hiveOverrides`. ✅\n- `/fix` handler — **was missing**; fixed here. ✅\n- `/task` handler — does not delegate to `/solve`, so no solve overrides apply. ✅\n- Direct CLI `fix` (outside Telegram) — `TELEGRAM_SOLVE_OVERRIDES` is a\n  Telegram-bot concept; the direct CLI already forwards user options to\n  `solve.mjs`. No change needed. ✅\n\nNo other delegation site omits the overrides.\n\n## 6. Existing components / libraries reviewed\n\n- **`mergeArgsWithOverrides` (internal, issue #1228).** The repo already had a\n  battle-tested override-merge helper for `/solve` and `/hive`. Rather than\n  writing something new, this fix promotes it to a shared module and reuses it.\n  This is the \"known existing component that solves a similar problem.\"\n- **yargs last-wins parsing** ([advanced docs](https://github.com/yargs/yargs/blob/main/docs/advanced.md)).\n  `solve.mjs`/`fix.mjs` parse with yargs, where the last occurrence of an option\n  wins. Appending overrides at the end of the arg list is therefore the correct,\n  documented way to guarantee they take precedence — matching the existing\n  helper's contract.\n- **`extractIsolationFromArgs` / `isValidPerCommandIsolation`** (internal). Reused\n  verbatim to handle an `--isolation` override consistently with `/solve`.\n\n## 7. Tests added\n\n- [`tests/test-args-overrides.mjs`](../../../tests/test-args-overrides.mjs) —\n  unit tests for the extracted `mergeArgsWithOverrides` (imports the real\n  module, not a replica).\n- [`tests/test-telegram-fix-command.mjs`](../../../tests/test-telegram-fix-command.mjs) —\n  new cases proving `/fix` applies solve overrides, that overrides win over a\n  conflicting user flag, that an `--isolation` override is honored, that a\n  per-command `--isolation` still applies, that an invalid override isolation is\n  rejected, and that the info block shows/omits the locked-options line.\n",

[2026-07-20T00:25:32.336Z] [STDOUT] ## Summary

Fixes #2085.

`/fix --ci-cd` **does** call the real `/solve` in a real working session — this
is proven by the captured solve-session metadata of the run cited in the issue,
PR #2083, whose `rawCommand` is a genuine `node .../src/solve.mjs …` invocation.
The actual defect is narrower: the Telegram bot's **operator solve overrides**
(`TELEGRAM_SOLVE_OVERRIDES`, e.g. `--attach-logs`) were merged into `/solve` and
`/hive` but **never into `/fix`**. So the solve launched by `/fix` ran without
the operator's configured defaults — exactly the "`--attach-logs` were not
applied" symptom.

Per #1733, `/fix` should behave as a straightforward combination of `/task` +
`/solve`. This PR makes `/fix` reuse the **identical** override mechanism
`/solve` already uses — no new/fancy machinery.

## Root cause

`mergeArgsWithOverrides()` lived inside `telegram-bot.mjs` and was only applied
by the `/solve` and `/hive` handlers. The `/fix` handler
(`telegram-fix-command.lib.mjs`) never received `solveOverrides`, so the
overrides were absent from the args forwarded to `solve.mjs`. The override must
be baked into the **arguments** (not read from env by `fix.mjs`) because Docker
isolation only forwards explicitly-listed `-e` env vars into the container, so a
Docker `/fix` session would never see `TELEGRAM_SOLVE_OVERRIDES`.

## Changes

- **`src/args-overrides.lib.mjs`** (new): shared `mergeArgsWithOverrides`
  extracted from `telegram-bot.mjs` (adds `Array.isArray` null-safety) so
  `/solve`, `/hive` and `/fix` share one implementation without a circular
  import on the bot entry point.
- **`src/telegram-bot.mjs`**: import the shared helper; pass `solveOverrides`
  into `registerFixCommand`.
- **`src/telegram-fix-command.lib.mjs`**: merge `solveOverrides` into the fix
  args (overrides win, appended last for yargs' last-wins parsing), honor an
  optional `--isolation` override from the overrides, validate the model on the
  merged args, and surface a `🔒 Solve overrides: …` line in the work-session
  info block.
- **Tests**: `tests/test-args-overrides.mjs` (new unit tests for the real
  helper) and new `/fix` override cases in `tests/test-telegram-fix-command.mjs`.
- **Case study**: `docs/case-studies/issue-2085/` — timeline, requirements,
  root-cause analysis, solution, codebase audit, and existing-components review,
  with primary evidence (`data/pr-2083-solve-metadata.json`).
- **Changeset**: patch bump.

## How to reproduce (before the fix)

1. Run the Telegram bot with `TELEGRAM_SOLVE_OVERRIDES="(\n  --attach-logs\n)"`.
2. Trigger `/fix <repo>`; it generates the CI/CD issue and starts `/solve`.
3. Inspect the started solve's `rawCommand` (session `metadata.json`): it lacks
   `--attach-logs` (see PR #2083's captured metadata). After this fix, the
   override is present.

## Verification

- `tests/test-args-overrides.mjs` — 8/8 pass.
- `tests/test-telegram-fix-command.mjs` — 28/28 pass (7 new override cases).
- `tests/test-issue-1228-options-deduplication.mjs` — 19/19 pass (no regression
  in existing override behaviour).
